From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
Performances by American actor
[![Photograph of Dwayne Johnson in 2013](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e2/The_ROCK_b.jpg/250px-The_ROCK_b.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:The_ROCK_b.jpg)Johnson in 2001
American actor and professional wrestler [Dwayne Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwayne_Johnson "Dwayne Johnson"), also known by his [ring name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ring_name "Ring name") The Rock, is one of the highest-paid and highest-grossing actors of all time.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwayne_Johnson_filmography#cite_note-1) His films have grossed over $3.5 billion in North America and over $12.5 billion worldwide.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwayne_Johnson_filmography#cite_note-2)
Johnson had his first acting role in 1999, when he appeared on the popular sitcom _[That '70s Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/That_'70s_Show "That '70s Show")_ , portraying his real-life father, Rocky Johnson, in the episode titled "That Wrestling Show". He made his first film appearance in _[The Mummy Returns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Mummy_Returns "The Mummy Returns")_ (2001) and reprised his role from that film for his first leading role in the spin-off _[The Scorpion King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Scorpion_King "The Scorpion King")_ (2002). He has since starred in numerous other successful films, including _[The Rundown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Rundown "The Rundown")_ (2003), _[Walking Tall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walking_Tall_\(2004_film\) "Walking Tall \(2004 film\)")_ (2004), _[Doom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doom_\(film\) "Doom \(film\)")_ (2005), _[Southland Tales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southland_Tales "Southland Tales")_ (2007), _[The Game Plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Plan_\(film\) "The Game Plan \(film\)")_ (2007), _[Get Smart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Get_Smart_\(film\) "Get Smart \(film\)")_ (2008), _[Race to Witch Mountain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_to_Witch_Mountain "Race to Witch Mountain")_ (2009), _[Tooth Fairy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tooth_Fairy_\(2010_film\) "Tooth Fairy \(2010 film\)")_ (2010), _[You Again](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You_Again "You Again")_ (2010), _[Journey 2: The Mysterious Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Journey_2:_The_Mysterious_Island "Journey 2: The Mysterious Island")_ (2012), _[G.I. Joe: Retaliation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G.I._Joe:_Retaliation "G.I. Joe: Retaliation")_ (2013), _[Pain& Gain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pain_&_Gain "Pain & Gain")_ (2013), _[Hercules](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hercules_\(2014_film\) "Hercules \(2014 film\)")_ (2014), _[San Andreas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Andreas_\(film\) "San Andreas \(film\)")_ (2015), _[Central Intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Intelligence "Central Intelligence")_ (2016), _[Moana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_\(2016_film\) "Moana \(2016 film\)")_ (2016), _[Rampage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rampage_\(2018_film\) "Rampage \(2018 film\)")_ (2018), _[Skyscraper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skyscraper_\(2018_film\) "Skyscraper \(2018 film\)")_ (2018), and _[Jungle Cruise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jungle_Cruise_\(film\) "Jungle Cruise \(film\)")_ (2021).
Johnson's most commercially successful role is as [Luke Hobbs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luke_Hobbs "Luke Hobbs") in the _[Fast& Furious](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast_&_Furious "Fast & Furious")_ franchise; he first appeared as the character in _[Fast Five](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast_Five "Fast Five")_ (2011) and is credited with breathing new life into the franchise, catapulting it into one of the highest-grossing movie franchises in history.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwayne_Johnson_filmography#cite_note-3) He starred in the sequels _[Fast& Furious 6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast_&_Furious_6 "Fast & Furious 6")_ (2013), _[Furious 7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Furious_7 "Furious 7")_ (2015), and _[The Fate of the Furious](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fate_of_the_Furious "The Fate of the Furious")_ (2017), as well as his own spin-off film _[Hobbs& Shaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hobbs_&_Shaw "Hobbs & Shaw")_ (2019) and a cameo in _[Fast X](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast_X "Fast X")_ (2023).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwayne_Johnson_filmography#cite_note-4) Another notable franchise starring Johnson is [_Jumanji_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jumanji_\(franchise\) "Jumanji \(franchise\)"), with the films _[Jumanji: Welcome to the Jungle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jumanji:_Welcome_to_the_Jungle "Jumanji: Welcome to the Jungle")_ (2017) and _[Jumanji: The Next Level](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jumanji:_The_Next_Level "Jumanji: The Next Level")_ (2019). He also provided the voice of [Maui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maui_\(Moana\) "Maui \(Moana\)") in the [Disney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney "Disney") animated films _[Moana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_\(2016_film\) "Moana \(2016 film\)")_ (2016) and _[Moana 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_2 "Moana 2")_ (2024), as well as portraying Maui in the [live-action _Moana_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moana_\(2026_film\) "Moana \(2026 film\)") (2026).
Johnson has also ventured into television, starring in the [HBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO "HBO") series _[Ballers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ballers "Ballers")_ (2015–2019), which ended its first season as HBO's most-watched comedy in six years.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwayne_Johnson_filmography#cite_note-5)
The filmography does not include his professional wrestling appearances in any form of media.
